title: Chemical Changes: pH Indicators, Neutralisation and Applications
topic: Chemical Changes - pH, Indicators and Real-World Applications
subject: Science

questions.question: A student tests four solutions with Universal Indicator. Solution P turns red, Solution Q turns green, Solution R turns purple, Solution S turns yellow. Which solution is neutral?
questions.explanation: Universal Indicator turns green in neutral solutions (pH 7). Red indicates strongly acidic, yellow indicates weakly acidic, and purple indicates alkaline.

questions.question: The table shows Universal Indicator colours for different pH ranges. A solution turns orange with Universal Indicator. What is its approximate pH range?
questions.explanation: Universal Indicator turns orange in weakly acidic solutions (pH 4-6). Red indicates strongly acidic (pH 1-3), green is neutral (pH 7), and blue/purple is alkaline (pH 8-14).

questions.question: A student tests a solution with both red and blue litmus paper. The blue litmus paper turns red, but the red litmus paper shows no change. What can be concluded about the solution?
questions.explanation: Blue litmus paper turns red in acidic solutions. Red litmus paper stays red in acidic solutions. This confirms the solution is acidic.

questions.question: A farmer tests the soil pH in his field. The soil turns Universal Indicator yellow. Which crop would grow BEST in this soil?
questions.explanation: Yellow with Universal Indicator indicates weakly acidic soil (pH 4-6). Potatoes grow best in acidic soil, while beans prefer neutral and spinach prefer alkaline conditions.

questions.question: Acid rain lowers the pH of soil. Which observation suggests acid rain has affected a field?
options: Soil turns Universal Indicator red or orange
questions.explanation: Acid rain makes soil more acidic. Universal Indicator turns red or orange in acidic conditions, indicating a lower pH.

questions.question: Some plants like blueberries grow better in acidic soil. If a farmer wants to grow blueberries, what should the soil pH be?
questions.explanation: Blueberries and some other crops prefer acidic soil (pH below 7). Farmers may add acidic materials to lower soil pH for these crops.

questions.question: A person has excess stomach acid causing discomfort. An antacid tablet containing calcium carbonate is taken. What type of chemical reaction occurs in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Antacids containing carbonates react with excess stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) in a neutralisation reaction to form salt, water and carbon dioxide, reducing acidity.

questions.question: An antacid contains calcium carbonate. Which word equation represents its reaction with stomach acid (hydrochloric acid)?
options: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide
calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + hydrogen
calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium + water + chlorine
questions.explanation: This is a neutralisation reaction: carbonate + acid → salt + water + carbon dioxide. Calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid to form calcium chloride, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Why should antacids not be taken in very large amounts?
options: They have no effect if taken in large amounts
They can make the stomach too alkaline, affecting digestion
They make the stomach too acidic
They cause combustion in the stomach
questions.explanation: Taking too much antacid can make the stomach too alkaline, which may interfere with normal digestion that requires some acid.

questions.question: A student tests rainwater with Universal Indicator. It turns yellow-orange. What does this suggest about the rainwater?
options: It is acidic, possibly due to acid rain
It is neutral and safe for plants
It is alkaline and good for soil
questions.explanation: Yellow-orange with Universal Indicator indicates acidic conditions (pH 4-6). This suggests the rainwater may be acid rain, which can harm the environment.

questions.question: Which statement about acid rain is correct?
options: Acid rain has no effect on the environment
Acid rain can lower soil pH, affecting which crops can grow
Acid rain only affects buildings, not soil or plants
Acid rain makes soil more alkaline, helping all crops grow
questions.explanation: Acid rain lowers soil pH (makes it more acidic), which can harm some crops but may benefit others that prefer acidic conditions.

questions.question: A wasp sting is alkaline. Which substance could be used to neutralise the pain?
questions.explanation: A wasp sting is alkaline. An acidic substance like vinegar can neutralise it through a neutralisation reaction, reducing pain.

questions.question: A bee sting is acidic. Which substance could be used to neutralise the pain?
questions.explanation: A bee sting is acidic. An alkaline substance like baking soda solution can neutralise it through a neutralisation reaction, reducing pain.

questions.question: Which observation would confirm that a solution is alkaline using litmus paper?
options: Blue litmus paper stays blue and red litmus paper stays red
Both litmus papers stay the same colour
questions.explanation: Red litmus paper turns blue in alkaline solutions. Blue litmus paper stays blue in alkaline solutions but turns red in acidic solutions.

questions.question: A student has three colourless solutions: acid, alkali, and water. Which test would BEST distinguish all three?
options: Test with red litmus paper only
Test with blue litmus paper only
questions.explanation: Universal Indicator shows different colours for acid (red/yellow), neutral (green), and alkali (blue/purple), allowing all three to be distinguished. Litmus paper only shows acid or alkali, not neutral.

questions.question: A farmer adds lime (calcium hydroxide) to acidic soil. What is the purpose of this?
options: To make the soil dry faster
To neutralise the acidity and raise the soil pH
To make the soil more acidic for certain crops
To add nutrients only, not change pH
questions.explanation: Lime is an alkali that neutralises acidic soil, raising the pH to a level more suitable for most crops. This is an application of neutralisation.

questions.question: Which statement about electrolysis is correct for Sec 2 level?
options: Electrolysis is the same as electroplating
Electrolysis uses an electric current to cause chemical changes
Electrolysis only works with solid substances
Electrolysis uses heat to break down compounds
questions.explanation: Electrolysis uses an electric current to cause chemical reactions, such as breaking down compounds or depositing metals in electroplating.

questions.question: Why might a gardener add compost to soil that has been affected by acid rain?
options: Compost makes soil dry out faster
Compost can help neutralise acidity and improve soil structure
Compost has no effect on soil pH
questions.explanation: Compost can help buffer soil pH, reducing the effects of acid rain. It also improves soil structure and adds nutrients, helping plants grow better.

questions.question: A student tests a solution with Universal Indicator. It turns blue. Which statement is correct?
options: The solution is acidic and will not change red litmus paper
The solution is alkaline and will turn red litmus paper blue
The solution is neutral and will not change either litmus paper
The solution is acidic and will turn blue litmus paper red
questions.explanation: Blue with Universal Indicator indicates an alkaline solution (pH 8-14). Alkaline solutions turn red litmus paper blue.

questions.question: An antacid tablet containing calcium carbonate is added to hydrochloric acid. The mixture fizzes and becomes less acidic. What has happened?
options: The acid has been completely used up in a neutralisation reaction
The antacid has dissolved without reacting
questions.explanation: Antacids containing carbonates react with acids in a neutralisation reaction. The fizzing is carbon dioxide gas being produced. When the acid is neutralised, the solution becomes less acidic or neutral.
